<!-- pr-reviewer: ca5a6826b80c75d0973852f04e8eff43b624758c -->

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

I reviewed the diff at head ca5a6826 against main 6f8b309d. The PR merges cleanly with main.

## What looks good

- The new `onRadiusCompensation` hook refuses every `COMP` record: left, right, wear, and a standalone OFF. The engine calls this hook for each `COMP` record (`crates/post/src/post/engine.rs:404-434`). Each refusal is a counted warning. It names the operation and the reason. It is not a silent skip.
- `sectionOk = false` suppresses the later cutting blocks in the section (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps:258`). A section that already threaded the wire still writes its `T90` cut at the section end (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps:325-332`). The program does not leave the wire threaded in the work.
- A `COMP OFF` cannot clear the refusal. The flag `controlOffset` stays set, and the section-open check `machineGood && !controlOffset` (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps:187`) carries a refusal that arrived before `SECTION` into the section.
- `onSectionEnd` resets `controlOffset` (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps:347`), so a later plain section still posts. The reset point is correct. The review found no case that drops a legal later cut, and no case that lets an unsafe cut through.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1498-sodick-control-offset.md`. It names what future support needs before the post enables the feature.
- The script keeps its provenance header, and it cites the Sodick manual and RS-274 only. The new test file carries a provenance line. It sits in `camcraft-post`, the lowest crate that provides what it imports.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` outside tests. No new crate dependency. No golden or snapshot file changed. The commit subject is conventional. The body has a `Changelog:` line.

## Results (built and run locally in a review worktree, debug)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (every suite) | Pass - 0 failures, includes all 7 `sodick_comp` pins |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test sodick_wire_post` | Pass - 9 tests |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wire_post` | Pass - 12 tests |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test sodick_alc400g` | Pass - 5 tests |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance` | Pass - 7 tests (each built-in posts its goldens byte-exact, Sodick included) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Pass |

The diff does not change `crates/app` source, so clippy did not run on that crate. Its Sodick suites ran because they post the changed script through the registry.

## Mutation check

I removed the section-end reset line `controlOffset = false;` and re-ran `sodick_comp`. The pin `sodick_comp_refusal_resets_for_the_next_plain_section` failed; the other six passed. The guard is pinned. I restored the file after the check.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `refuse()` dedupes by the key `offset` + operation name. If one operation sends `COMP` records in two separate sections, the second section is still suppressed but adds no new warning. The first warning already blocks the release, so the result stays visible. This matches the script's other keyed refusals.
- No physical Sodick control ran the output. The script's standing header note "NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL" still tells the operator to check before cutting.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
